stem: Kirtan Sohila is a short bani of five hymns on Angs 12–13 of the Guru Granth Sahib. According to the Sikh Rehat Maryada, at what time of day is it recited?
options: at dawn, during the amrit vela
at night, before going to sleep
at midday, before the main daily meal
at sunset, together with Rehras
why: The Sikh Rehat Maryada sets Rehras for the evening and Kirtan Sohila for night, before going to sleep. It is also recited when the Guru Granth Sahib is put to rest and at a cremation.
source: Sikh Rehat Maryada, ch. 3 (nitnem); Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 12–13

es.stem: Kirtan Sohila es una bani corta de cinco himnos, en los Ang 12–13 del Guru Granth Sahib. Según el Sikh Rehat Maryada, ¿a qué hora del día se recita?
options: al amanecer, durante el amrit vela
de noche, antes de irse a dormir
al mediodía, antes de la comida principal
al atardecer, junto con el Rehras
es.why: El Sikh Rehat Maryada pone el Rehras al atardecer y el Kirtan Sohila de noche, antes de dormir. También se recita cuando el Guru Granth Sahib se lleva a descansar y en la cremación.

stem: In Guru Nanak's hymn "Gagan mai thaal" (Raag Dhanasari, sung in Kirtan Sohila), the sky is the platter, the sun and moon are the lamps and the stars are the pearls. What is the hymn describing?
options: the heavens the soul crosses after death
the first day on which the world was made
the aarti all creation offers the Creator
the night sky over Guru Nanak's last journey
why: Gagan mai thaal (Dhanasari, Mahala 1, Ang 13) pictures the whole universe performing aarti, the lamp offering, to the Creator: the breeze is the incense, the forests the flowers, and one light shines in all.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 13, Raag Dhanasari, Mahala 1

es.stem: En el himno de Guru Nanak "Gagan mai thaal" (Raag Dhanasari, cantado en Kirtan Sohila), el cielo es la bandeja, el sol y la luna son las lámparas y las estrellas son las perlas. ¿Qué describe el himno?
options: los cielos que cruza el alma tras la muerte
el primer día en que fue hecho el mundo
el aarti que toda la creación ofrece al Creador
el cielo nocturno del último viaje de Guru Nanak
es.why: Gagan mai thaal (Dhanasari, Mahala 1, Ang 13) pinta el universo entero haciendo aarti, la ofrenda de lámparas, al Creador: la brisa es el incienso, los bosques son las flores, y una sola luz brilla en todo.

stem: Sukhmani Sahib, the "jewel of peace," begins on Ang 262 of the Guru Granth Sahib in Raag Gauri. Which Guru composed it?
options: Guru Nanak
Guru Angad
Guru Ram Das
Guru Arjan
why: Sukhmani is headed Gauri Sukhmani Mahala 5: it is the work of Guru Arjan, the fifth Guru, who also compiled the Adi Granth.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 262, Gauri Sukhmani, Mahala 5

es.stem: Sukhmani Sahib, la "joya de la paz", comienza en el Ang 262 del Guru Granth Sahib, en Raag Gauri. ¿Qué Gurú la compuso?
options: Guru Nanak
Guru Angad
Guru Ram Das
Guru Arjan
es.why: Sukhmani lleva el encabezado Gauri Sukhmani Mahala 5: es obra de Guru Arjan, el quinto Gurú, que también compiló el Adi Granth.

stem: In Sukhmani Sahib's fifth ashtpadi, a banker lends a man his capital, then takes a little of it back, and the man flies into a rage. What does Guru Arjan use this picture to teach?
options: all we have is God's trust, to give back without anger
a debt to a lender has to be repaid with full interest
wealth comes from a person's own hard work and effort
God punishes all those who waste what they have been given
why: Sukhmani, ashtpadi 5: the one who rages when the lender takes back his own loses his credit; the wise one places the owner's thing before the owner, accepts the order with bowed head, and is made four times happier.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Sukhmani ashtpadi 5 (Raag Gauri)

es.stem: En la quinta ashtpadi de Sukhmani Sahib, un prestamista le presta su capital a un hombre, luego le pide de vuelta una parte, y el hombre se enfurece. ¿Qué enseña Guru Arjan con esta imagen?
options: todo lo que tenemos es un préstamo de Dios, para devolverlo sin enojo
una deuda con un prestamista se paga con todos sus intereses
la riqueza viene del propio trabajo y esfuerzo de cada persona
Dios castiga a quienes malgastan lo que se les ha dado
es.why: Sukhmani, ashtpadi 5: quien se enfurece cuando el prestamista recupera lo suyo pierde su crédito; el sabio pone lo del dueño delante del dueño, acepta la orden con la cabeza inclinada y es cuatro veces más feliz.

stem: In Sukhmani Sahib's twelfth ashtpadi, Guru Arjan says that as long as a person thinks "something gets done by me," no peace comes to them. Which of the five thieves of Gurbani is he naming?
options: kaam, lust of the senses
karodh, anger in the mind
lobh, greed for still more
ahankaar, ego and pride
why: Sukhmani, ashtpadi 12: "jab lag jaanai mujh te kachh hoe, tab is kau sukh naahee koe": while one believes things are done by oneself, there is no peace. That is ahankaar, or haumai, ego; the ashtpadi's salok praises the humble.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Sukhmani ashtpadi 12 (Raag Gauri)

es.stem: En la duodécima ashtpadi de Sukhmani Sahib, Guru Arjan dice que mientras alguien piense "algo se hace por mí", no le llega la paz. ¿Cuál de los cinco ladrones del Gurbani está nombrando?
options: kaam, la lujuria de los sentidos
karodh, la ira en la mente
lobh, la codicia de más y más
ahankaar, el ego y el orgullo
es.why: Sukhmani, ashtpadi 12: "jab lag jaanai mujh te kachh hoe, tab is kau sukh naahee koe": mientras uno crea que las cosas se hacen por sí mismo, no hay paz. Eso es ahankaar, o haumai, el ego; el salok de la ashtpadi alaba a los humildes.

stem: A carpenter earns his bread by fair, hard labor, never by cheating or exploiting anyone, like Bhai Lalo in the janamsakhis. Which of the three pillars of Sikh life does this describe?
options: naam japna, remembering God
vand chhakna, sharing with all
kirat karni, honest toil
dasvandh, giving a tenth
why: The three pillars taught from Guru Nanak's time are naam japna, kirat karni (living by honest work of one's own) and vand chhakna (sharing). Dasvandh, giving a tenth, is a practice, not one of the three.
source: Janamsakhi story of Bhai Lalo and Malik Bhago; Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1245

es.stem: Un carpintero se gana el pan con trabajo justo y duro, sin engañar ni explotar a nadie, como Bhai Lalo en las janamsakhis. ¿Cuál de los tres pilares de la vida sij describe esto?
options: naam japna, recordar a Dios
vand chhakna, compartir con todos
kirat karni, el trabajo honrado
dasvandh, dar la décima parte
es.why: Los tres pilares enseñados desde Guru Nanak son naam japna, kirat karni (vivir del propio trabajo honrado) y vand chhakna (compartir). El dasvandh, dar la décima parte, es una práctica, no uno de los tres.

stem: Besides bedtime, on which occasions is Kirtan Sohila recited, and what do those occasions have in common?
why: Kirtan Sohila is recited when the Guru Granth Sahib is put to rest at night (sukhasan) and at a cremation, followed by Ardas. Each one closes something: a day, the scripture's day in the gurdwara, a life.
source: Sikh Rehat Maryada (nitnem; funeral ceremonies); Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 12–13

rubric.point: Names the cremation or funeral of a Sikh as an occasion for Kirtan Sohila. 'At a death' or 'at the end of a life' counts.
Says what the occasions share: each is a closing or a rest (of a day, of the scripture's day, of a life). Saying only 'they are sad' does not count.
Names the putting to rest of the Guru Granth Sahib at night (sukhasan) as an occasion (optional, strengthens). 'At the end of the gurdwara day' counts as partly.

es.stem: Además de la hora de dormir, ¿en qué ocasiones se recita Kirtan Sohila, y qué tienen en común esas ocasiones?
es.why: Kirtan Sohila se recita cuando el Guru Granth Sahib se lleva a descansar de noche (sukhasan) y en la cremación, seguido del Ardas. Cada ocasión cierra algo: un día, el día de la escritura en el gurdwara, una vida.

stem: At Anandpur on Vaisakhi 1699, after Guru Gobind Singh initiated the Panj Pyare with amrit, what did he do next, and why is it remembered?
why: The Guru asked the five to initiate him with amrit in the same way. The teacher took initiation from his own disciples, so Guru and Khalsa are bound both ways; a later verse calls him "aape gur chela," himself the Guru and the disciple.
source: Vaisakhi 1699, Anandpur; Var 41 attributed to Bhai Gurdas

rubric.point: Says the Guru asked the Panj Pyare to give him amrit, or was initiated by them in the same way. 'He joined the Khalsa' without saying the five initiated him counts as partly.
Says why it matters: the teacher took initiation from his own disciples, so Guru and Khalsa are bound both ways or stand as equals. Either wording counts.
Mentions the phrase 'aape gur chela' (himself Guru and disciple), or that he became Gobind Singh then (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: En Anandpur, en el Vaisakhi de 1699, después de que Guru Gobind Singh iniciara con amrit a los Panj Pyare, ¿qué hizo a continuación, y por qué se recuerda?
es.why: El Gurú les pidió a los cinco que lo iniciaran con amrit de la misma manera. El maestro recibió la iniciación de sus propios discípulos, así que el Gurú y el Khalsa quedan unidos en ambos sentidos; un verso posterior lo llama "aape gur chela", él mismo Gurú y discípulo.
